text: The Bronze streaming job from a few videos back works -- but working in a demo and surviving a real production restart are different bars. This video closes that gap.

Four changes make it production-grade: a durable checkpoint on a Unity Catalog Volume, maxOffsetsPerTrigger to bound any post-outage backlog, and schema enforcement that quarantines a bad event instead of crashing the stream.

The checkpoint now lives somewhere durable and access-controlled, and maxOffsetsPerTrigger caps how much a single micro-batch pulls -- so a backlog after downtime doesn't risk an out-of-memory failure.
A malformed event -- a buggy firmware update, say -- gets routed to its own quarantine table instead of silently vanishing or taking the whole job down. Both streams get their own checkpoint.
A deliberate kill-and-restart test confirms no events were lost or duplicated by the restart itself. Next: Git and CI start checking every change before it ships.
